Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

effective adjective

also effectual, ineffective, have an effect, have no effect

classical

Sen. Ep. 6.5: breve et efficāx per exempla
Liv. 1.9 (Lewis & Short)

efficāx, efficācis

adjective, third declension; with ad, adversus or the dative

effective, effectual

Mostly post-Augustan; not in Cicero or Caesar, though Caelius uses it in a letter to Cicero (Fam. 8.10.3) (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • valeō, valēre, valuī, valitum — to have force, to work, to be effective

    verb, second conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.17.1: valēbunt autem semper arma (Lewis & Short)

    First “be strong, be well”; transferred, “have power, prevail, avail”.

  • prōficiō, prōficere, prōfēcī, prōfectum — to achieve something; nihil prōficere, to have no effect

    verb, third conjugation (-iō) · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 7.20: sī nihil in oppugnātiōne oppidī prōfēcisset (Lewis & Short)

    Also “make progress”, and of things “be of use”.

Examples

  • longum iter est per praecepta, breve et efficāx per exempla

    the road through rules is long; through examples it is short and effectiveSen. Ep. 6.5

  • amāra cūrārum ēluere efficāx

    good at washing away the bitterness of caresHor. C. 4.12.20 (Lewis & Short)

  • Hoc medicāmentum adversus tussim efficāx est.

    This medicine is effective against a cough.composed

See also efficient, useful, powerful.
